origin: it should NOT report expected code
source:
defmodule CredoSampleModule do
  def some_function(parameter1, nil) do
    something
  end
  def some_function(parameter1, parameter2) do
    something
  end
  # `is_nil` in guard still works
  def common_guard(%{a: a, b: b}) when is_nil(b) do
    something
  end
end

origin: it should NOT report a violation - `not is_nil is not part of a guard clause`
source:
defmodule CredoSampleModule do
  def some_function(%{parameter1: parameter2, id: id}) when is_binary(parameter2) do
    something = not is_nil(parameter2)
  end
end

origin: it should report only one violation in a module with multiple functions when only one is problematic
source:
defmodule CredoSampleModule do
  def hello(a) when not is_nil(a), do: a
  def foo1(x) when is_integer(x), do: x
  def foo2(x) when is_integer(x), do: x
end

origin: it should report two violations in a module with multiple functions when two are problematic
source:
defmodule CredoSampleModule do
  def hello(a) when not is_nil(a), do: a
  def foo1(x) when is_integer(x), do: x
  def foo2(x) when is_integer(x), do: x
  def hello2(a) when not is_nil(a), do: a
  def foo3(x) when is_integer(x), do: x
